# max-length-not-enforced

- Dialects: mysql, postgres, sqlite
- Default: on

## Why

The model promises a string never exceeds a length, and validation in the application is the only thing keeping that true unless the database also refuses longer values. A column without a limit (TEXT, unbounded VARCHAR) or with a larger one accepts whatever another writer or a bug stores, and the model's assumptions about size (UI, indexes, downstream limits) break later.

## Fix

Keep the maximum length in the model and regenerate the migration: it should use a length-limited type (VARCHAR(n) or CHAR(n) on PostgreSQL and MySQL) or a CHECK on the length (char_length(col) <= n; length(col) <= n on SQLite). Trim or fix existing longer values first.

## Exception

A limit that the model enforces only for input validation while the column is intentionally wider, for example during a staged migration; write the reason down. SQLite ignores the n of VARCHAR(n), so only a CHECK counts there.

The same text is printed by `schemalens explain max-length-not-enforced`. An exclusion needs a written reason. Back to the [rule index](README.md).
